Acme.description:
How certificates are issued and which node issues them. the daemon's `acme` module reads
every field.

account_key_pem.description:
PKCS#8 PEM key of the ACME account, so every restart and every issuer node uses the same
account. Absent: the issuer creates a fresh account in memory.

challenges.description:
HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01 answers the control plane pushes back after an `acme_challenge`
event. Every node serves the HTTP-01 ones on the plain HTTP listener and answers the
TLS-ALPN-01 ones on the TLS listener.

contact.description:
Contact URIs of the account, such as `mailto:ops@example.com`. Used when podgate creates
the account itself; ignored with `account_key_pem`.

dns_ready.description:
DNS-01 TXT records the control plane has published and sees on the zone's authoritative
servers, pushed back after `acme_challenge` events of type `dns-01`. The
issuer tells the CA to validate a challenge only once it is listed here.

eab.description: External account binding for CAs that require one. Excludes `account_key_pem`.

issuer_node.description:
`NODE_NAME` of the one node that orders certificates. Every other node ignores the
ordering fields and only serves `challenges`.

requested_hosts.description:
Hosts the control plane asks the issuer to get certificates for: the hosts of
`certificate_requested` events it approved. Only hosts of `on_demand` apps count.

App.description:
One app: the unit of tenancy and deployment. It owns its routers, middlewares, services and
transports; every name resolves inside the app only.

allow_domain_fronting.description:
Serve TLS requests whose `Host` differs from the SNI. Absent: refuse them
with `421`.

canary.description:
Ramp one serving revision up while it stays healthy, and pull it back when it does not
. Absent: revisions share traffic by their weights.

declared_by.description: Free text naming the source of this declaration; used in errors and explain output.

default_chain.description: Names of middlewares that run before every router's own chain.

forwarded.description:
Which forwarding headers the app's upstreams receive. Absent: the default set,
[`Forwarded::default`].

middlewares.description: Middlewares routers may name in their `chain`.

record_bodies.description:
Keep request and response bodies (up to 64 KiB) of failed requests for replay.
Absent: record headers only.

revisions.description: Deployed revisions, split by weight and state.

routers.description: Routers: what the app answers for and where each request goes.

scale_to_zero.description:
Let the app sleep with no upstreams and wake on its first request. Absent:
a request to an app with no upstream gets `503`.

services.description: Services shared by every revision. A revision's own services are in [`Revision::services`].

tcp.description: TCP routers and services. Not built yet.

transports.description: Upstream transports services may name. Not built yet.

max_buffer_bytes.description: Most bytes of proxy memory the tenant may buffer.

max_inflight.description: Most requests the tenant may have in flight.

Canary.description:
Canary policy of an app: the rollout of one revision, judged by its own `5xx` rate.

The snapshot owns the policy; podgate owns the live share at runtime (see `crate::canary` in
the daemon).

interval_secs.description: Seconds between two judgments, at least `1`.

max_error_permille.description:
At this many `5xx` per thousand requests of the canary, or more, it is pulled back to
`0`. `1..=1000`.

revision.description:
The canary's [`Revision::id`]; it must be `serving`. Its own `weight` is ignored: the
canary's share replaces it.

step_percent.description:
Percent of new sessions the canary gains per healthy interval, `1..=100`. It is also the
share the canary starts with.

Certificate.description: A certificate chain and its private key, served for the listed hosts.

default.description:
Serve this certificate for a name no other certificate covers, and for a handshake with
no SNI, unless the app that owns the name sets `sni_strict`. At most one.

hosts.description: Hosts the certificate answers for: exact names or `*.` wildcards.

key_pem.description: PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1 private key, PEM.

ocsp.description:
OCSP stapling: `auto` (default), `on` or `off`. The responder always comes from the
certificate itself, never from the snapshot.

Challenge.description:
One challenge answer pushed back after an `acme_challenge` event. Exactly one of `token`
(HTTP-01: `GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>` returns `key_authorization`) and `name`
(TLS-ALPN-01: the host that an `acme-tls/1` handshake proves with a challenge
certificate over `key_authorization`) is set.

key_authorization.description: The key authorization to answer with.

name.description: The host of a TLS-ALPN-01 challenge.

ChallengeKind.description: The ACME challenge the issuer answers for an `acme` app's hosts.

oneOf.description: Answered over plain HTTP by every node; cannot prove a wildcard.

Answered with a TXT record the control plane publishes; proves wildcards and hosts
that cannot serve plain HTTP.

Answered on the TLS listener with a challenge certificate, so only port 443 must be
reachable; cannot prove a wildcard.

ClientAuthMode.description: Whether and how clients are asked for a certificate (Traefik's `clientAuthType`).

oneOf.description: Ask for a certificate; serve clients with none and trust none.
Require some certificate; the chain is not judged.
A certificate, when sent, must chain to `client_ca_pem`; none is fine.
A certificate that chains to `client_ca_pem` is required.

Declared.description:
A kind-tagged, named object: a middleware, service or transport.

The envelope only knows the name and the type; the module of that type owns the rest and
parses it strictly.

name.description: Unique among the app's objects of this kind of object.

DnsReady.description:
One published DNS-01 TXT record. Carries no credential: it names a record that is already
public.

value.description:
The record's value: base64url of the SHA-256 of the key authorization. It tells apart
the challenges of an apex and its wildcard, which share one name.

EntryPointPolicy.description: The policy for the entry point called `name`.

allow_encoded_slash.description:
Accept an encoded `/` (`%2F`) in the path. It is kept as an escape inside its segment,
never turned into a separator. A posture change in a plan.

max_header_bytes.description: Largest request head (request line and headers) in bytes.

name.description: The entry point this policy is for; the process must have bound it.

proxy_protocol.description:
`{trusted_ips, insecure}`: the peers allowed to send a PROXY protocol header to an entry
point started with `;proxy_protocol` (`docs/ref/proxy-protocol.md`). Neither field set
trusts nobody. `insecure: true` trusts every peer and is a posture change in a plan.

redirect.description: `{to, permanent}`: answer every request with a redirect to the entry point `to`.

tenants.description:
Tenants that may attach routers to the entry point. Absent: every tenant. A router with
no literal host that lists an entry point whose `tenants` names only its own tenant may
match any host there.

timeouts.description:
`{read_secs, write_secs, idle_secs, header_secs}`: each is applied or refused with
`unsupported_setting` (`docs/ref/entry-policy.md`).

underscore_headers.description: What to do with request headers whose name holds an underscore. Absent: `keep`.

ExternalAccount.description: External account binding credentials, as a CA hands them out.

Forwarded.description:
The forwarding headers an app's upstreams receive. Every field is optional; an absent one has
the default below, so `{}` is the same as no object at all.

rfc7239.description: Also write the RFC 7239 `Forwarded` header. Default `false`.

server.description:
Write `X-Forwarded-Server` with the node's name. Default `false`: the header tells the
app which host proxies it, which it does not need.

Observability.description: Snapshot-wide observability settings; a router may override them per router.

access_log.description:
Structured access log: `format`, `fields`, `headers`, `filters`, `sampling_percent`; a
boolean switches it off or on with the defaults. Absent: nothing is logged.

metrics.description: Per entry point, router and service metrics.

tracing.description: OpenTelemetry tracing: sample rate, propagation, recorded headers.

OcspMode.description: Whether podgate staples an OCSP response to a certificate.

oneOf.description:
Staple only when the certificate carries the TLS Feature `status_request` (must-staple)
extension.

Staple whenever the certificate names an OCSP responder in its Authority Information
Access.
Never staple.

Revision.description: One deployed version of an app.

services.description: The services of this release. A router's service is looked up here first.

state.description: Whether the revision takes new traffic.

weight.description: Share of new traffic against the app's other serving revisions.

RevisionState.description: Lifecycle state of a revision; see `docs/architecture.md` (`### Revision states`).

oneOf.description: Gets new sessions by weight.
Gets no new sessions; still serves pinned ones.
Gets no new requests; in-flight requests finish.

Router.description: One router: a matcher, a middleware chain and a service.

chain.description: Names of middlewares that run after the app's `default_chain`, in order.

declared_by.description: Source of this router when it differs from the app's.

entry_points.description: Entry points the router listens on. Absent: every HTTP and HTTPS entry point.

observability.description:
Per-router observability overrides: `{"access_log": false}` silences the router, `true`
logs it. Metrics and tracing overrides are not built yet.

priority.description:
Higher goes first among the routers of one tenant. Absent: `0`. Never orders routers of
different tenants.

service.description: The service that answers, by name: one of the revision's services, else one of the app's.

idle_secs.description: Seconds without a request after which the app is reported idle (`app_idle`).

wake_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a request waits for the app to wake before it gets `503`.

SkewSecret.description:
The HMAC key for session cookies: the snapshot's `skew_secret`. Never printed: `Debug` hides it.

Any string deserializes; the daemon's snapshot compiler refuses one shorter than
[`Self::MIN_LEN`].

Tcp.description: The TCP side of an app.

id.description: Unique id; apps name it in [`App::tenant`].

oneOf.description: Issued for the app's declared hosts.
Issued at the first handshake for a matching host.

TlsPolicy.description: How an app gets certificates, plus optional client authentication.

alpn.description:
The ALPN protocols a connection to this app may negotiate: `h2` and `http/1.1`. Absent:
both.

challenge.description: How the issuer proves the app's hosts to the CA. Absent: `http-01`.

cipher_suites.description:
The cipher suites a connection to this app may negotiate, by rustls name. Absent: every
suite of the listener.

client_auth.description:
How client certificates are asked for and judged. Absent: `require_and_verify`
when `client_ca_pem` is set, no client authentication otherwise.

client_ca_pem.description: PEM of the CA that must sign client certificates. Absent: no client authentication.

curves.description: Not enforceable per app: the compiler rejects it with `unsupported_setting`.

http3.description:
Whether HTTP/3 may serve this app. Absent: yes, unless the app has a
`client_ca_pem` or `client_auth`, `cipher_suites`, or an `alpn` without `h2`, which HTTP/3
cannot honour. `true` together with one of those is rejected with `unsupported_setting`.
Only matters on an HTTPS entry point with the `;http3` option.

max_version.description: Not enforceable per app: the compiler rejects it with `unsupported_setting`.

min_version.description: Lowest TLS version a connection to this app may have. Absent: the listener's floor.

pass_client_cert.description:
Removed in change 0055; a snapshot that sets it to `true` is rejected with
`unsupported_setting`, which names the `pass_tls_client_cert` middleware as the
replacement. `false` and absent are accepted and mean nothing.

session_tickets.description: Not enforceable per app: the compiler rejects it with `unsupported_setting`.

sni_strict.description:
Refuse a handshake for a name of this app that has no certificate, instead of serving the
default certificate.

oneOf.description: TLS 1.2.
TLS 1.3.

Udp.description: The UDP side of an app.

UnderscoreHeaders.description:
What an entry point does with a request header whose name holds an underscore (`X_Forwarded_For`),
which a CGI-style upstream may read as `X-Forwarded-For`.

oneOf.description: Pass the header on. What an entry point with no policy does.
Remove the header and serve the request.
Answer `400` and serve nothing.

matcher.description: A matcher tree: an object with exactly one key, a leaf or a combinator.

matcher.alpn.description: TCP routers only: the ClientHello offers one of these application protocols.

alpn.description: An ALPN protocol name, or a list of them.

matcher.client_ip.description: The resolved client address is in one of these blocks.

client_ip.description: An address or CIDR block, or a list of them.

matcher.header.description: A request header is present, with the value when given.

header.description: The header `name` and, optionally, its exact `value`.

matcher.header_regexp.description: A request header's value matches a regular expression.

header_regexp.description: The header `name` and a Rust `regex` pattern.

matcher.host.description: The request's host, without port: an exact name or a `*.` wildcard, or a list of them.

host.description: A host name or `*.` wildcard, or a list of them.

matcher.host_regexp.description: The host matches a regular expression. It only narrows a literal `host` claim.

matcher.method.description: The request method is one of these.

method.description: An HTTP method, or a list of them.

matcher.path.description: The normalized path is exactly this.

matcher.path_prefix.description: The normalized path is this or under it, at a segment boundary.

matcher.path_regexp.description: The normalized path matches a regular expression.

matcher.query.description: A query parameter is present, with the value when given.

query.description: The parameter `name` and, optionally, its exact `value`.

matcher.query_regexp.description: A query parameter's value matches a regular expression.

query_regexp.description: The parameter `name` and a Rust `regex` pattern.

matcher.sni.description: TCP routers only: the server name in the ClientHello is an exact name or a `*.` wildcard, or a list of them. Claims the names like `host`.

sni.description: A host name or `*.` wildcard, or a list of them.

matcher.sni_regexp.description: TCP routers only: the server name in the ClientHello matches a regular expression. It only narrows a literal `sni` claim, like `host_regexp`.

header_field.description: A request header that receives the user name; a value the client sent for it is replaced.

realm.description: The realm of the challenge; default `podgate`.

remove_header.description:
Remove `Authorization` before the request goes to the upstream; default `false`, as in
Traefik.

users.description:
htpasswd entries, `user:hash`, with a bcrypt (`$2a$`, `$2b$`, `$2y$`) or argon2
(`$argon2id$`, `$argon2i$`, `$argon2d$`, PHC form) hash.

buffer_request.description:
Holds the whole request body before the upstream request starts. Needs
`max_request_body_bytes`, at most [`MAX_BUFFERED_REQUEST_BYTES`].

buffer_response.description: Holds the whole response body before the client gets it. Needs `max_response_body_bytes`.

max_request_body_bytes.description: Largest request body, in bytes; a larger one is refused with `413`.

max_response_body_bytes.description:
Largest response body, in bytes; a larger one is refused with `502`. Needs
`buffer_response`.

middleware.cache.description: The declaration of a `cache` middleware. Every field is optional; see `docs/ref/mw-cache.md`.

cache_set_cookie.description:
Store a `Set-Cookie` response with the cookie removed from the stored copy; default
`false`: such responses are never stored.

collapse_timeout_ms.description:
How long a request waits for the fetch another request leads, in milliseconds;
default 3000, at most 10000.

default_ttl_secs.description: Freshness for a response that names none; absent: only explicit freshness is stored.

ignore_request_cookies.description: Serve and store for requests that carry `Cookie`; default `false`: they bypass the cache.

max_bytes.description:
Most bytes the tenant's cache may hold when this middleware stores; default a quarter of
the tenant's `max_buffer_bytes`, at most the operator's `CACHE_TENANT_MAX_PERCENT`.

max_object_bytes.description: Largest response kept, in bytes; default 1 MiB or `max_bytes`, whichever is lower.

max_stale_secs.description: Longest the response's own `stale-while-revalidate` and `stale-if-error` are honoured.

max_ttl_secs.description: Longest an entry stays fresh, in seconds; default 86400.

normalize_query.description: Sort the query parameters before they are part of the key; default `false`.

share_across_revisions.description: Share entries between the revisions of the app; default `false`.

statuses.description: Statuses that may be stored; default `200 203 204 301 308 404 410`.

tag_header.description: The response header that lists purge tags (for example `Cache-Tag`).

middleware.cache.title: Config

check_period_ms.description: How often the closed circuit is judged, in milliseconds. Default `100`.

fallback_secs.description: How long the circuit stays open, in seconds. Default `10`.

min_requests.description: Fewest requests a window needs before it can trip the circuit. Default `20`.

recovery_secs.description:
How long traffic takes to return from 0 to 100%, in seconds. Default `10`; `0` closes the
circuit as soon as the fallback is over.

response_code.description:
The status of the answer while the circuit is not letting a request through. Default
`503`.

trip_when.description: What opens the circuit; any one of the triggers does.

latency_quantile_ms.description:
Trips when a latency quantile of the window is above a limit. Traefik's
`LatencyAtQuantileMS(q) > ms`.

ms.description:
Trips above this many milliseconds. The quantile is estimated from a histogram whose
buckets are 25% wide and read at the middle of the bucket, so it is off by up to 12%.

quantile.description: The quantile as a percentage, `0..=100`: `50.0` is the median, `99.0` the 99th percentile.

network_error_ratio.description:
Trips when more than this share of the window's requests ended in a network error: the
upstream could not be reached or failed before it answered. Traefik's
`NetworkErrorRatio() > r`. `0..=1`.

response_code_ratio.description:
Trips when responses in one status range are more than a share of those in another.
Traefik's `ResponseCodeRatio(from, to, over_from, over_to) > r`.

from.description: First status of the counted range.

over_from.description: First status of the range it is measured against. Default `0`.

over_to.description: One past the last status of the range it is measured against. Default `600`.

to.description: One past the last status of the counted range.

header_field.description: A request header that receives the user name; a value the client sent for it is replaced.

qop.description: Only `auth` is accepted; `auth-int` needs the body and is refused.

realm.description: The realm of the challenge; default `podgate`.

remove_header.description:
Remove `Authorization` before the request goes to the upstream; default `true`. The
upstream has no use for a digest response, and one it could replay is not worth handing
out.

users.description:
htdigest entries, `user:realm:HA1`, where `HA1` is `hex(H(user:realm:password))`: 32 hex
digits for MD5, 64 for SHA-256. The realm of every entry is the middleware's `realm`.

allow_origins.description:
Origins allowed to call from a browser: exact `scheme://host[:port]`, or `*` for any.
Absent or empty: no CORS headers and no preflight answer.

cors.description: CORS; absent means the middleware does nothing about `Origin`.

add_vary.description: Add `Vary: Origin` to responses that depend on the origin. Default `true`.

allow_credentials.description: `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`; refused together with the `*` origin.

allow_methods.description: `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`; absent means the header is not sent.

allow_origin_regexes.description: Regular expressions an origin must match entirely.

allow_origins.description: Allowed origins, exact (`scheme://host[:port]`), or `*` for any.

request.description: Edits to the request on its way to the upstream.

set.description: Header name to value. An empty value is refused: removal is `remove`.

response.description: Edits to the upstream's response, and the security headers.

hsts.description: `Strict-Transport-Security`, added to responses of TLS connections only.

max_age_secs.description: `max-age`, in seconds; `0` tells browsers to forget the policy.

source.description: A `source` as written in a snapshot.

oneOf.description: The client address under an `ipStrategy`.

ip.description: A `source.ip` as written in a snapshot: Traefik's `ipStrategy`, plus the IPv6 prefix.

items.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR block such as `10.0.0.0/8`.

ipv6_subnet_bits.description: Prefix length an IPv6 client is counted by; default [`DEFAULT_IPV6_SUBNET_BITS`].

oneOf.description: The first value of a request header.
The host of the request; only `true` is valid.

items.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR block such as `10.0.0.0/8`.
An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR block such as `10.0.0.0/8`.

keys.description: An inline JWK set, `{"keys": [...]}`; the only place a symmetric (`oct`) key may be.

items.description: A string or a number or a boolean: what a required claim is compared with.

anyOf.description: A string or a number or a boolean: what a required claim is compared with.

additionalProperties.description: One value, or a list of which one must match.

items.description: A place a token may be in: one of `header`, `cookie`, `query`.

header.description: A request header; with `scheme`, the value is `<scheme> <token>`.

query.description: A query parameter. A token in a URL is logged by every proxy on the way: avoid it.

scheme.description: The authentication scheme of a `header`; `Bearer` for `authorization`.

client_secret.description: A secret. `Debug` shows nothing of it.

items.description: A string or a number or a boolean: what a required claim is compared with.

anyOf.description: A string or a number or a boolean: what a required claim is compared with.

additionalProperties.description: One value, or a list of which one must match.

same_site.description: The `SameSite` attribute of the session cookie.

info.description: Send these fields in `X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert-Info`. Absent: no info header.

issuer.description: `Issuer`: the selected parts of the issuer name.

serial_number.description: `SN`: the issuer's own serial number attribute.

not_after.description: `NA`: the end of the validity, in Unix seconds.

not_before.description: `NB`: the start of the validity, in Unix seconds.

sans.description: `SAN`: DNS names, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and URIs, `,` separated.

subject.description: `Subject`: the selected parts of the subject name.

serial_number.description: `SN`: the subject's own serial number attribute.

local_fallback.description: The limit a node applies alone while its store is unavailable.

anyOf.description: What a request does when the store gives no verdict.

oneOf.description: Admit it if the local fallback bucket allows it.
Refuse it with `503`.
This node alone (the default).
Every node that shares the store.

source.description: A `source` as written in a snapshot.

oneOf.description: The client address under an `ipStrategy`.

ip.description: A `source.ip` as written in a snapshot: Traefik's `ipStrategy`, plus the IPv6 prefix.

items.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR block such as `10.0.0.0/8`.

ipv6_subnet_bits.description: Prefix length an IPv6 client is counted by; default [`DEFAULT_IPV6_SUBNET_BITS`].

oneOf.description: The first value of a request header.
The host of the request; only `true` is valid.

replacement.description: The target, with `$1`, `${1}`, `$name` and `${name}` for groups.

port.description: The port to redirect to; a port that is the scheme's default is not written in the URL.

scheme.description: The scheme to redirect to: `http` or `https`.

replacement.description: What replaces each match; `$1`, `$name` and `${name}` insert capture groups.

attempts.description: Attempts including the first, 1 to 5. `1` never retries.

initial_interval_ms.description:
Wait before the first retry, in milliseconds; each further retry waits twice as long.
Default `100`, at most `10000`. `0` retries at once.

methods.description:
Methods retried after a reused connection died. Default: `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`,
`PUT`, `DELETE`, `TRACE`. A connect failure is retried for any method.

prefixes.description: Prefixes, each starting with `/`; the first one that matches is removed.

regexes.description:
Regular expressions (Rust `regex` syntax, unanchored); the first that matches a non-empty
text at the start of the path is removed.

fuel.description: Instructions the filter may execute per request; running out ends the request with `500`.

max_memory_bytes.description:
Most bytes of linear memory the filter may hold; growing past it ends the request with
`500`.

wasm_base64.description: The module in the WebAssembly binary format, standard base64.

fallback.description: The service that takes them otherwise: `name` or `name@revision`.

fallback_hold_secs.description:
How long the fallback keeps serving after the primary was last seen without a healthy
server, default 10, at most 3600.

service.description:
The service that takes requests while it has a healthy server: `name` or
`name@revision`.

algorithm.description: The balancing algorithm: a name, or an object `{"type": name, ...options}`. Absent: `round_robin`.

oneOf.description:
The object form of `algorithm`: the name as `type`, and the options of the algorithms that
have any.

health_check.description: The fields of a `health_check`, as written.

anyOf.description: How the host of a server's URL is resolved.

oneOf.description: `A` and `AAAA` records: the host is a server name and the URL carries the port.

An `SRV` record: the host is the full owner name (`_web._tcp.shop.service.consul`), the
URL has no port, and the targets, ports, priorities and weights come from DNS.

url.description:
`http://host:port` or `https://host:port`. `host` is an IP address or a DNS name, which
podgate resolves again on the record's TTL and checks against the upstream address
policy on every answer. With `resolve: "srv"` it is `http://owner.name` without a port.

max_body_size.description:
The most body bytes that are mirrored, default 1 MiB, at most 16 MiB. Larger bodies are
not mirrored. Needs `mirror_body`.

mirror_body.description: Send the request body to the mirrors too (default `false`).

mirror_timeout_secs.description: How long one copy may take in all, default 10, at most 60.

percent.description: The share of requests copied, `0` to `100`, down to four decimals.

service.description: A `loadbalancer` of the same app: `name`, or `name@revision`.
The service every request goes to: a `loadbalancer` of the revision, else of the app.

services.description: The children and their relative weights.

service.description:
A `loadbalancer`, `weighted` or `failover` service of the app: `name`, or
`name@revision`.

weight.description: Relative weight, `0` to `65535`; `0` never receives a request.

sticky.description: Pins a client to one child by cookie.

tcp.router.description: The configuration of a TCP router.

chain.description:
Names of the app's TCP middlewares (`ip_allow_list`, `in_flight_conn`), run in this order
before the connection is routed to a server, the tenant takes a slot or a server is dialled.

entry_points.description: The `tcp` entry points the router listens on; each is reserved to the app's tenant.

name.description: Unique among the app's TCP routers.

service.description: The TCP service that takes the connections.

tls.description:
`{"passthrough": true}` forwards the TLS stream untouched; `{}` terminates TLS with the
app's certificates. Absent: the router does not look at TLS (and cannot match `sni`,
`sni_regexp` or `alpn`).

passthrough.description:
Forward the encrypted stream to the server untouched; the server completes the
handshake. Default `false`: podgate terminates TLS and forwards plain bytes.

tcp.router.title: RouterConfig

amount.description: Connections one source may hold open at once, at least 1.

max_sources.description: Sources the table holds, 1 to 1,000,000; default 10,000.

anyOf.description: A `source` of `in_flight_conn`: only the address exists at layer 4.

oneOf.description: The peer address, an IPv6 one counted by its first `ipv6_subnet_bits` bits.

ipv6_subnet_bits.description: Prefix length an IPv6 peer is counted by, 1 to 128; default 64.

source.description: What counts as a source. Absent: `{"ip": {}}`, the peer address.

tcp_middleware.ip_allow_list.description: The configuration of an `ip_allow_list` middleware on a TCP router.

source_range.description: The blocks, CIDR or single addresses, IPv4 and IPv6, 1 to 4096 of them.

items.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR block such as `10.0.0.0/8`.

tcp_middleware.ip_allow_list.title: IpAllowListConfig

health_check.description: Active probe of each server; absent: none. See `docs/ref/l4-health.md`.

expect.description:
Base64 of the bytes (1 to 256) the reply must start with. Without `send`, the server
speaks first (a banner).

healthy_threshold.description: Consecutive passes that mark a down server up: 1 to 100, default 1.

interval_secs.description: Seconds from the end of one probe to the start of the next: 1 to 3600.

port.description: Probe this port of the server's IP instead of the server's own port.

send.description: Base64 of the bytes (1 to 256) written after the connect.

send_proxy_header.description: Write a PROXY protocol v2 `LOCAL` header first.

timeout_secs.description: A probe that has not finished by then fails: 1 to 300.

tls.description:
Probe over TLS with the service's transport; the probe passes on a completed handshake
(and the reply, when `expect` is set). Not with `send_proxy_header`.

unhealthy_interval_secs.description: Seconds between probes of a server that is marked down: 1 to 3600. Absent: `interval_secs`.

unhealthy_threshold.description: Consecutive failures that mark an up server down: 1 to 100, default 1.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds without a byte in either direction before the connection is closed: 1 to 86,400,
default 300.

proxy_protocol.description:
Write a PROXY protocol header, `{"version": 1|2}`, first on every connection to a server:
the client's real address and the entry point's. Absent: none.

version.description: `1` writes the text line, `2` the binary header.

address.description:
`host:port`: an IP literal (`10.0.0.5:5432`, `[2001:db8::5]:5432`) or a DNS name
(`db.internal:5432`). With `resolve: "srv"`, the full SRV owner name without a port
(`_db._tcp.shop.service.consul`): the records choose the targets and ports.

oneOf.description: An IP literal, or a name looked up for `A` and `AAAA` records.
A name looked up for `SRV` records.

resolve.description: `a` (the default): `address` is `host:port`. `srv`: `address` is an SRV owner name.

tls.description:
Reach the server over TLS, with the service's `transport` (SNI, CA, client certificate).
Default `false`: plain TCP.

weight.description:
Relative weight, `1` by default; only `weighted_round_robin` and `hrw` take one. Not
allowed with `resolve: "srv"`: the records carry the weights.

termination_delay_ms.description:
Milliseconds the server's side of a connection lives on after the client half-closed, so a
late reply is not cut: 0 to 86,400,000, default 100.

transport.description:
The `servers_transport` of the app that reaches the servers with `tls: true`. Only its TLS
fields and `dial_timeout_secs` apply to a TCP service.

transport.servers_transport.description:
The fields of a `servers_transport`, but for `client_cert`, which [`client_cert`] reads by
hand so that no parse error quotes the key.

client_cert.description: The certificate chain (leaf first) and private key, PEM, presented to a server that asks for one.

dial_timeout_secs.description: TCP connect and TLS handshake, in seconds.

http2.description: Offer `h2` to an `https://` server by ALPN (default true); false offers only HTTP/1.1.

idle_timeout_secs.description: How long an unused pooled connection is kept, in seconds.

max_idle_per_host.description:
Always refused with `unsupported_setting`: Pingora's pool has no per-host cap, see the
`UPSTREAM_POOL_SIZE` setting.

max_stream_lifetime_secs.description: The longest a tunnel lives, in seconds (1..=86400). Default: unlimited.

proxy_protocol.description: A PROXY protocol header on every new connection to the servers: `{"version": 1|2}`.

version.description: `1` writes the text line, `2` the binary header.

read_timeout_secs.description: Wait for the response head, then for each read of the body, in seconds.

stream_close_delay_secs.description:
How long a tunnel lives on after its server was removed by a snapshot, in seconds
(1..=86400). Default: unlimited.

tunnel_idle_timeout_secs.description: How long a tunnel may be idle, in seconds (1..=86400). Default: unlimited.

write_timeout_secs.description: Each write of the request, in seconds.

transport.servers_transport.title: Config

udp.router.description: The configuration of a UDP router.

entry_points.description: The `udp` entry points the router listens on; each is reserved to the app's tenant.

max_reply_ratio.description:
Until a client has sent a second datagram, the most bytes returned to it, as a multiple of
its first datagram's bytes: 1 to 1000. Absent: no limit.

max_sessions.description: Sessions held per entry point: 1 to 65,536, default 4096.

name.description: Unique among the app's UDP routers.

udp.router.title: RouterConfig

servers.description: The servers, as IP literals; 1 to 256.

session_timeout_secs.description: Idle seconds before a session expires: 1 to 3600, default 30.

description: The complete desired state of one node. Replaces the previous snapshot as a whole.

acme.description:
ACME issuance settings. Absent: no certificate is ordered; only
`certificates` are served.

certificates.description: Certificates served on the TLS listener, chosen by SNI. Change 0014 fills this from ACME.

entry_points.description: Request-time policy per entry point. Absent: the defaults of every entry point.

observability.description: Access log, metrics and tracing settings. Absent: the process defaults.

revert_window_secs.description:
Seconds after this snapshot goes live during which a 5xx spike in the apps it changed
restores the previous snapshot. Absent: 60. `0`: never revert. Capped at 300.

skew_secret.description:
Key that signs the session cookie pinning a browser to a revision, at least 16
bytes (a shorter one rejects the snapshot with `422`). Absent: skew protection is off. Never
logged.

version.description: Strictly increasing; a snapshot not newer than the live one is refused.
